Principal Product Marketing Manager, AI Governance
Regulatory Counsel, AI Regulation, US
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY

reading.body:
Four AI governance openings at Cohere, Databricks, Anthropic, and ServiceNow show the work splitting into policy, legal, marketing, and cloud cost control rather than one compliance function.

The four titles describe four different jobs. Cohere wants a Global Public Policy Manager for Compute, Infrastructure and Sovereign AI, remote in the United States. Anthropic wants Regulatory Counsel for US AI regulation in San Francisco or New York. Databricks wants a Principal Product Marketing Manager for AI governance. ServiceNow wants a Staff FinOps AI Governance Lead in Santa Clara. Governance is the shared label, not the shared task.

Two of the four connect governance to compute and money. The ServiceNow role sits in FinOps, where governance means watching what cloud capacity costs. The Cohere title treats compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI as policy subjects, which puts government buildout plans inside a policy job description. If governance is enforced through cost controls and procurement, then some of the people constraining what models run are the people tracking the bill, not lawyers.

The data covers four postings and nothing more. There is no salary, no count over time, and no comparison against other AI functions. Posting dates run from April to September 2026, so this is not a burst of hiring. All four come from company career boards rather than the aggregators listed alongside them. Nothing here shows whether governance hiring is growing, shrinking, or typical.
